**STEP 1 - Scene:** A single slice of bread (white or sourdough-style, with an open crumb and a browned crust) on a plate. There is no other food visible.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** A white square-ish dinner plate, about 26 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** One bread slice. No butter, spread, or oil is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The slice covers roughly 28% of the plate (about 148 cm²). Only about 28% of the vessel is covered by food.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** A bread slice is about 1.5 cm thick on average. 148 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 220 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** The protocol's 0.9–1.0 g/ml bread density is for dense items. Airy bread has a bulk density closer to a loaf's (~0.3 g/ml), so I used 0.3. 220 ml × 0.3 ≈ 65 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Bread is about 260 kcal/100 g. 65 g × 2.6 ≈ 169 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A single slice of bread weighing about 65 g and about 170 kcal is plausible. A full dinner plate would hold far more, but this plate holds only one slice.

Total: about 65 g, about 170 kcal.
